itineraries.title: Atacama to Uyuni in a week
itineraries.summary: The desert of San Pedro, then three days by jeep across the red and green lagoons of Bolivia to the salt flat of Uyuni.
itineraries.season_note: All year. April, May and September to November are the sweet spot; June to August is clear and very cold at night up high. December to March is the rainy season on the plateau and in Salta: the salt flat turns into a mirror, and the lagoon tracks can close for a day after heavy rain.

stops.name: San Pedro de Atacama
plan: Arrive and settle in. Stargazing in the desert.

High lagoons and Piedras Rojas.
do: Sleep: In San Pedro; all tours pick up there. Cash helps: few cash machines.
Dress in layers you peel off: −10 °C at dawn, 25 °C by noon.
Swimwear under the clothes for the pool.

stops.name: Laguna Colorada
plan: Arrive. Laguna Verde, the Dalí desert, Polques and Laguna Colorada.

do: Sleep: Basic shared shelters: near Laguna Colorada at about 4,300 m, no heating; the second night in a village or a salt hotel near the salt flat. A sleeping bag rated −10 °C, or rent one in San Pedro or Uyuni.
Keep to the hard ground: the crust around the pools is thin.

itineraries.title: Iceland in a week: the south coast and the glacier lagoon
itineraries.summary: The Golden Circle from Reykjavik, the waterfalls and black beaches of the south coast, Jökulsárlón, and back.
itineraries.season_note: June to August: 18-24 hours of light, 10-15 °C. October to April: 4-10 hours of light, storms can close the south coast road for a day, ice caves November to March, northern lights September to April. This week works all year.

stops.name: Reykjavik
plan: Arrive and settle in. Reykjavík on foot: Hallgrímskirkja, Harpa, the Old Harbour.
The Golden Circle: Þingvellir, Geysir, Gullfoss.
do: Sleep: Downtown near Laugavegur, on foot to everything; tours pick up at numbered bus stops.
Snorkel Silfra, the rift full of glacier water at Þingvellir, in a drysuit: book ahead.
Lunch among tomato plants at the Friðheimar greenhouse: book a table.
Strokkur's spray drifts with the wind: stand upwind.

stops.name: Vík í Mýrdal
plan: Arrive. Seljalandsfoss, Gljúfrabúi and Skógafoss on the way.
Glacier walk on Sólheimajökull, Dyrhólaey, Reynisfjara.
do: Sleep: Vík, or a farm between Skógar and Vík.
You get soaked behind Seljalandsfoss: waterproof trousers too, not just a jacket.
Reynisfjara's sneaker waves kill: stay well back from the water, watch the warning lights.
Part of Dyrhólaey closes in the nesting season (May to late June).

excursions.title: Glacier walk on Sólheimajökull, Dyrhólaey, Reynisfjara

stops.name: Skaftafell
plan: Arrive. Skaftafell: Svartifoss and the glacier tongue.
Jökulsárlón, the iceberg lagoon, and Diamond Beach. Glacier walk on Falljökull.
do: Sleep: Near Skaftafell or Jökulsárlón to be first at the lagoon; Höfn has the most beds and restaurants.
Seals fish in the channel under the bridge: look down from the lagoon side.

itineraries.title: Vietnam in three weeks: the far north and the Mekong
itineraries.summary: The north at its best, the Ha Giang Loop, Sapa, Mai Chau, Ninh Binh and Ha Long, then Saigon and the Mekong Delta, skipping the flooded centre.

itineraries.title: Vietnam in four weeks, from Ha Giang to the Mekong
itineraries.summary: The whole country: the Ha Giang Loop and Sapa, Ninh Binh and Ha Long, the caves of Phong Nha, Hue, Hoi An, Saigon and the Mekong Delta.
itineraries.season_note: February to April is the best all round. In October and November the centre (Hue, Hoi An, Phong Nha) has its floods and some caves close: keep those days flexible. December and January are cold in the far north; May to September hot and wet, with typhoons.
